shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Four vanilla-matched per-level sizes (126/190/250/300) and level counts are bought from a fixed 192,000-cell budget. Per-colony climate bands make high levels genuinely alpine. Content on lower levels draws smaller once per level of drop, which is what makes a deep column read as depth.
body:
> **NOTE TO SELF:** this body is a running spec, not a changelog. Sections 1-19 are the architecture; §20 is the third-party compat library. Keep every ⚠ - each one cost a run to learn.

# As above, So below II (V2)

> V1 is DELETED. ~72 files, ~20,500 LOC. No em-dashes anywhere in shipped text; keep it that way.

## Pitch
Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`. Priorities in order: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

## Status
Visuality, QOL, altitude/weather and settings passes are all VERIFIED IN PLAY. **Seven-level maps generate clean: 4.1 s for 7 bands (run #207), 3.2 s for 4 bands (run #206).**
UNVERIFIED IN PLAY: below-snow, the depth shrink (§6g), the new-game camera anchor (§8a), the whole §18 audit, the Map Preview reroll grid (§6d-REROLL), **all four §20 compat patches**, and **the new size tiers + preview Clamp fix (§2, §6d-CLAMP)**.

**⚠ TWO LIVE BUGS REPORTED FROM THE PUBLISHED BUILD.** One diagnosed and fixed (preview, §6d-CLAMP). One **NOT DIAGNOSED**: fog and rocks appear to regenerate on save reload (§21). Do not patch §21 before running the discriminating observation.

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount * Slot)`. Bands stack along +z from the deepest basement, with a permanently-fogged gutter between them. `Slot = ceil((bandHeight + MinGutter) / 64) * 64`; **64-alignment of SLOT is load-bearing** (terrain shaders sample by world position). Per-level sizes 126 / 190 / 250 / 300.

**The one insight.** `Region.Neighbors` is *topological, not spatial*. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms, temperature or vacuum, and `Reachability.CanReach` works unpatched. But reachability is not a path: 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

**Hard 1.6 constraints.** The path grid is an IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell, so total stacked cells is the runtime metric. No `PathFinder.FindPath`. `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

**⚠ The stack is 2x to 7x anisotropic.** Anything vanilla normalises by BOTH map dimensions is distorted, and that bug class cannot appear on an ordinary square map.

### ⚠ THE SLICING RULE, six shapes
| Shape | Example | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor, a point picked as a fraction of `Size.z` | river and lake centre; random/edge cell (§15a); VEE Crater jitter (§20) | remap the point |
| Field, a gradient centred on the map centre | coastline (§6e); **VEE LoneIsland and Crater (§20)** | re-centre the sample coordinate |
| Noise space, a slice is not a short map | Map Preview (§6d); **GL landform grids (§20, OPEN)** | generate at full height, then crop |
| Distance-to-extent, a margin measured off `Size` | `CloseToEdge`, no-build edge (§15b, §15d); **river WIDTH (§20)** | re-base onto the cell's own band rect |
| **Aspect ratio, normalised by BOTH dims** | preview window AND reroll grid (§6d) | lay out from the BAND, generate at the STACK |
| **Map-wide scalar**, one per-tick value for the whole map | snow melt (§7), temperature readout (§16), **GL landform roof sweep (§20)** | rewrite it per cell at the consumer |

Classify a new bug into one of these six, but PROVE it. Still unaudited: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley (all use `FalloffAtAngle`).

**`ABBandLocal.cs` is THE canonical implementation of the FIELD rewrite** (`z' = (z % Slot) + (Size.z - bandHeight)/2`) plus `BandLocalModule`, a `ModuleBase` wrapper for consumers that sample a noise field directly instead of through a patchable method. Extracted from the coast prefix the moment a third consumer appeared.

# 2. LEVEL PLAN, budget 192,000 cells

## ⚠ THE 64 CONSTRAINT IS ON *SLOT*, NOT ON BAND HEIGHT
`Slot = ceil((bandHeight + 2)/64)*64` must be 64-aligned; the band height itself only has to leave `MinGutter` rows under that boundary. The original tiers were all 64k-2 (126/190/254) - the *tightest* fit - and **that coincidence was mistaken for the requirement for months**, which is what kept vanilla's own numbers off the list. 64k-2 is the CHEAPEST point, not the only legal one.

| size | slot | gutter | cells/band | playable | max levels | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 126 | 128 | 2 | 16,128 | 98.4% | 7 (cap) | 112,896 |
| 190 | 192 | 2 | 36,480 | 99.0% | 5 | 182,400 |
| **250** | 256 | 6 | 64,000 | 97.7% | 3 | **192,000** |
| **300** | 320 | 20 | 96,000 | 93.8% | 2 | **192,000** |

250 and 300 are vanilla's Medium and Large **exactly**. Paying 2.3% / 6.3% of cells buys numbers players recognise.

**The budget is tuned, not guessed:** 192,000 is simultaneously `3 x 64,000` and `2 x 96,000`, so both large tiers land dead on it, and `6 x 190`, `4 x 250`, `3 x 300` are all refused. Ladder is 7/5/3/2, monotone, and **every tier still yields real z-levels** - which is why 350 (134,400/band) and 382 (146,688/band) are NOT offered: a second level costs more than the whole budget, making them a z-mod option with no z.

**⚠ 200 IS THE ONE NUMBER TO AVOID.** It lands just PAST the 192 boundary: slot 256, gutter 56, 51,200 cells for 40,000 playable, 21.9% wasted - the worst point on the curve. **Waste is a SAWTOOTH in size, not a smooth function.** Recompute the table before adding any size.

**⚠ A WIDE GUTTER IS A FEATURE, NOT PURELY WASTE.** §14 records that "a spatial helper that reaches 22 rows will cross a 2-row gutter" - the root of §15a and §4. The gutter is 6 rows at 250 and 20 at 300, so those tiers are materially harder to punch through. Those cells were being rounded away to slot alignment regardless; this spends them on safety.

**Old saves are safe.** `bandHeight` is scribed per map and `SlotFor` is generic, so a 254 colony keeps loading even though 254 is no longer offered.

Per-level size is SQUARE, which is why `GenStep_Scatterer.CountFromPer10kCells` (it squares `Size.x`, not `map.Area`) already yields a per-BAND count. Only `GenStep_AnimaTrees` and `GenStep_TerrainPatches` read `map.Area`. **Squareness is also a repair tool:** `Size.x == bandHeight`, so foreign code that wrongly uses `Size.z` to mean "one level" can be corrected by substituting `Size.x` (§20, VEE Crater).

**⚠ The level chooser is also the lab.** `0 above / 0 below` generates an ORDINARY single-level map, the vanilla control. **STILL UNVERIFIED: does `0 up / 0 down` actually reach generation?**

**⚠ The chooser UI: own the widget, do not patch the data.** `Dialog_AdvancedGameConfig.MapSizes` is `static readonly` and the reflection swap SILENTLY FAILED in play. Our own radio buttons write `GameInitData.mapSize` directly - **which is also why `mapSize` is the authoritative record of the player's choice, and why nothing should ever re-derive it (§6d-CLAMP).** Window grown via an `InitialSize` postfix; **adding a size tier means growing that number too** (now +288f for four rows).
**⚠ The chooser LATCHES global state, and the release is a `Finalizer`.** `BeginChooser` sets `inChooser` (which gates a patch on `Listing_Standard.RadioButton`, a primitive every mod's settings window uses) and swaps the static `MapSizes` array. That release used to sit in the Postfix's `finally`, which does not run when VANILLA throws - see §18a.
**The level spinners are NOT known to be broken.** Run #190's "wrong plan" was USER ERROR, confirmed. **The plan PERSISTS between colonies.**

# 3. CROSS-BAND MOVEMENT
Segmented at ONE interception: `StartPath` prefix, tick sweep, `Carry` re-issues `StartPath`. `ABWormhole.TryGetTransit` BFSes the band graph; hops must strictly decrease. **Multi-hop routing STILL UNTESTED IN PLAY.**

# 4. GROUP ORDERING
`RecomputeDestinations` spreads the selection along the drag line, which between bands runs through the GUTTER. The odd/even signature ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 do not") is the proof, because only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5. Fix normalises `start`/`end` into the commanded pawns' band. Verified.

# 5. ⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE: `ABBands.TryResolveVisibleBelow`
Descends while each level is see-through, stops at the first opaque floor or the bottom band, returns the accumulated drop. TEN systems share it. **EIGHT separate appearances of the single `- Slot` bug** (the eighth found by the §18 audit, in the lighting overlay, written as INDEX arithmetic so the standing `grep '- Slot'` audit could not see it).

**`ABBands.TryResolveVisibleFrom` is now THE gate.** It folds the four-question preamble every caller was hand-rolling - in bounds, band > 0, out of the gutter, own terrain see-through - onto the descent, plus an optional unfogged check. Six passes are on it. Two legitimate exceptions: `SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` needs the "in bounds but fogged" distinction for its air mask and fog fan, and the upward-shape consumers (`ABBelowDynamicDraw`, `ABBelowOverlays`, `ABBelowMultiSelect`, `ABBelowSelectionDraw`) ask "is THIS thing what the column shows" and translate before descending.

Sun-shadow subtlety: its mask is neighbour-based, so mask and descent are answered together by `TryResolveDropAround`, taking the smallest drop among the nine cells.
Still single-band AND unshrunk: the realtime-things pass in `ABBelowDynamicDraw` (motes, fire, frames, projectiles).

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION (verified)
Four rejected attempts on record: force-linked wall masks, high-queue cover, wall-sprite suppression, and theorising twice about "flat" mountains before running the below-layer report.
Despeckle (walls dissolve only at 7+ open neighbours; at 6 it ate the outermost wall row off every meadow edge), one central fog hole, five-terrain plateau palette, cliff faces, alpine pass.
**⚠ The mass tapers with altitude, so +3 may contain NO LAND AT ALL.** Check for ground before diagnosing anything about the top level.
Ore glyph bug: ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`, so a "can't happen" fallback drew the whole atlas sheet per cell.

# 6a. ⚠ THE BELOW VIEW IS A SET OF MIRRORED PASSES, NOT ONE RENDERER
`SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` is a faithful port of vanilla `SectionLayer_Terrain` **and nothing else**. Every OTHER vanilla pass that contributes to how ground looks needs its own mirror. Confirmed twice: **Water** (§6b) and **Snow** (§6f).
Existing mirrors: BelowV2 (terrain + things + fog fan), BelowLighting, BelowShadows, BelowEdgeShadows, BelowWatergen, BelowSnow, MountainCap.

**⚠ THE CONVERSE IS ALREADY HANDLED, AND KNOWING WHY MATTERS.** A foreign mod that injects geometry during `Thing.Print` (ReGrowth's wall-snow postfix does exactly this) prints into whatever `SectionLayer` is passed - including ours, which are ordinary `SectionLayer` instances and indistinguishable to a foreign patch. That geometry is nonetheless correct in our view, because `SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` brackets the call as `SnapshotVertCounts()` -> `t.Print(this)` -> `FinishNewVerts(drop, centre, shrink)`, and **`FinishNewVerts` transforms by VERTEX RANGE, not by knowing which graphic emitted what**. Preserve that property: a rewrite that transforms per-graphic silently loses third-party compat.

**Cross-band invalidation is solved by `Patch_MapDrawer_ABMirrorDirtyUp`, and it obeys an ASCENT RULE.** It mirrors every dirty flag verbatim to bands above, so a new mirrored layer costs one `relevantChangeTypes` line. **It used to climb to EVERY band unconditionally, the inverse of §5.** The climb now stops at the first opaque floor, tested over the cell AND its eight neighbours (the mirrored passes are neighbour-sampling). The FIRST step stays unconditional because `SectionLayer_ABMountainCap` derives from exactly one Slot below regardless of transparency. Also mirrors vanilla's `ProgramState != Playing` guard (§18b).

**⚠ THE UNIT OF WASTE HERE IS A SECTION REGENERATION, NOT A CELL.** Seven of our layers plus vanilla's ten rebuild per dirtied section, so an unbounded mirror multiplied every mined rock by bandCount. Steady-state fps never showed it; it lands entirely in the hitches during mining and construction.

**⚠ SIX PASSES SHARE THE BELOW VIEW.** Any future per-frame geometry transform must be applied to ALL of them from one definition.

# 6b. ⚠ WATER: 1.6 water is a TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE effect
`SectionLayer_Watergen` (vanilla, `internal`, cannot be subclassed) is `SectionLayer_Terrain` plus `waterDepthMaterial`, drawn to the WaterDepth SUBCAMERA's layer. The visible `Map/TerrainWater` material samples that texture at its own SCREEN position.
- Water missing from upper levels, FIXED: `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` overrides `DrawLayer` to target `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`.
- Rivers not generating, FIXED: remap `GetRiverCenter` (not `Init`, which consumes it immediately). `GetLakeCenter` needs the same patch or it undoes the first.
- **River WIDTH is now clamped too** (§20). The centre was remapped years before the extent measured off it was - the same slicing-rule row appearing twice in one subsystem.

# 6b-LAKE. CLOSED: surface streaking accepted as vanilla appearance
PROVEN in run #173: a tile with water but no water mutators still streaked. **The ghost-river theory is dead.** Found en route: vanilla's flow builder ends `zero /= (float)num3` with no zero guard, writing NaN into a bilinear-filtered texture.

# 6c. DUBS MINT MINIMAP (verified)
ONE RECT, not seven patches. `DrawTextureFitted` preserves the TEXTURE's aspect, so use `ScaleMode.StretchToFill`. Reflection only.

# 6d. MAP PREVIEW (m00nl1ght.MapPreview)
Never calls `MapGenerator.GenerateMap` - it builds a bare Map and runs a short genstep list on a background thread, so our banding prefix never fires. **Generate at the full stacked height and crop via `TexCoords`**, because the surface band is a SLICE of a taller noise field. `MaxMapSize.z` MUST rise (default 500, a stack reaches 896). Most of it uses their public hooks, not Harmony.

## 6d-CLAMP. ⚠ THE PUBLISHED BUG: PREVIEW ONLY WORKED AT 190x190
Reported from the published build, diagnosed by inspection, FIXED, unverified in play.

`MapPreviewCompat.Stacked()` answered "how big will this map be?" by running the incoming size through `ABMapSizeLimit.Clamp()`. **`Clamp` is not an identity snap** - it returns *the largest offered size ≤ input that fits at the current level count*. And Map Preview passes **VANILLA's** configured map size (250 by default), not our per-level pick:
```
Clamp(250) at 4 levels -> 254 excluded (>250), 190 fits -> 190
lastBandHeight = 190
TryBandRows(stackedZ): BandCount * SlotFor(190) == stackedZ ?
   player chose 190 -> true  -> crop works
   anything else    -> false -> "not one of ours" -> no crop, broken
```
So the preview generated a 190-based stack **regardless of what the player selected**, and only agreed with reality when they happened to pick 190.

**The fix is `ABMapSizeLimit.PlannedSize`, and the distinction it draws is the lesson.** `Clamp` answers "sanitise this arbitrary number DOWN to something affordable" - correct for a value arriving from a scenario or stale config, and LOSSY by design. It was being used to answer a completely different question: "what did the player choose?" That was never a derivation problem - the chooser writes `GameInitData.mapSize` directly (§2), so the answer is simply on record. `PlannedSize` reads it and falls back to `Clamp` only for genuinely unknown values.
Also fixed alongside: `Stacked` clamped x and z INDEPENDENTLY, though a band is square, so the two could disagree; and `FixWindowAspect` re-Clamped `lastBandHeight` instead of trusting it.

**⚠ MAP PREVIEW SHIPS IN TWO HALVES, AND GEOLOGICAL LANDFORMS BUNDLES ONE.** `MapPreview.dll` (engine: `MapSizeUtility`, `DetermineMapSize`, `MapPreviewWidget`, `MapPreviewAPI`) is bundled by BOTH, byte-identical, so Lunar's version arbitration has no wrong answer. But `MapPreviewWindow` and `MapSeedRerollWindow` live ONLY in `MapPreviewMod.dll`, which GL does not ship.
**Consequence: with GL installed and Map Preview NOT installed, `MapPreviewCompat.Active` is TRUE while the window and reroll types are ABSENT.** Correct today only because every target is null-guarded independently. **Do not "simplify" `Active` into a single gate.**

## 6d-REROLL. THE SEED REROLL GRID (UNVERIFIED IN PLAY)
Their seed reroll (OFF by default) opens `MapSeedRerollWindow`, a grid of candidate previews.

**The seed needs NOTHING from us.** Preview seeds come from `MapPreviewRequest.SeedFromWorldSeed` -> `SeedRerollData.GetMapSeed`; the real map's seed is adjusted by a TRANSPILER on `MapGenerator.GenerateMap`. Same store, both sides; we only change SIZE, which is orthogonal.

**⚠ WHAT WAS BROKEN: the window opened COMPLETELY EMPTY.** `PreOpen` correctly takes the STACKED size, but `UpdateElementSize` shapes each thumbnail as `y = width / mapSize.x * mapSize.z`:
```
126x896 stack, 2560px window, 6 per row
  elementSize.y = 403 / 126 * 896 = 2,866 px   (a 7:1 sliver)
  gridSize.y    = floor(1330 / 2886) = 0
  DesiredCount  = 0  ->  trim loop disposes every element
  TryAddElement -> `if (_elements.Count >= DesiredCount) return;` -> 0 >= 0 -> returns
```
**The SECOND consumer of the stacked size caught out by it** - the first was their main preview window. Fixed by a postfix on `UpdateElementSize` that re-derives `_elementSize.y` from the BAND height, recomputes `_gridSize.y`, and kicks `TryAddElement` once. A POSTFIX repairing two statics, not a reimplementation.
- **Rejected: suppressing our inflation while the window is open** - every thumbnail would picture a map that will never generate.
- **Cropping is free:** `OnPromiseResolved` copies `result.TexCoords`, so the existing crop patch trims each thumbnail.
- **Accepted cost:** ~451 KB per Element at stacked size, up to ~60 in a grid, ~27 MB of which 6/7 is cropped. Transient; shrinking it means overriding `TextureSize` and roughly doubles the patch surface.
- `_elementSize` / `_gridSize` are STATIC, so a second open reuses corrected values. Harmless.

# 6e. COASTS (verified)
CENTRED wrong, not scaled wrong. `z' = (z % Slot) + (map.Size.z - bandHeight) / 2`, NO SCALING - stretching band-local z skews any non-axis-aligned field and makes displacement noise anisotropic.
**⚠ "Nine coastal mutators, none override `GetNoiseValue`" is about VANILLA ONLY.** Mods subclass `TileMutatorWorker` directly and declare their OWN virtual by that name. VEE's LoneIsland family is exactly that case and it drowns the colony (§20). The rewrite now lives in `ABBandLocal.TryRemap`; this patch is its reference caller.

# 6f. BELOW-SNOW (`SectionLayer_ABBelowSnow.cs`, UNVERIFIED IN PLAY)
Snow lying on a lower level was invisible from above. Not masking, not translation, not the descent rule: **no mirror of `SectionLayer_Snow` existed**.
**The near-miss that hid it:** `CellTerrainAt` genuinely samples `map.snowGrid.GetDepth(below)`, but `CellTerrain`'s snow coverage is consumed only by `MaterialFor`, to pick the POLLUTED variant. The right value read for an entirely different purpose.
**Why it was simpler than the terrain mirror:** vanilla's snow layer emits no per-cell geometry - ONE solid 9-verts-per-cell grid, only vertex COLOURS rewritten, depth in alpha. Our section already sits in the viewing band, so only sampled cells move. No vertex fix-up, no `- Slot`.
Details: geometry built once and reused (NOT `ClearSubMeshes(All)`); iteration order must match `MakeBaseGeometry` (x outer, z inner, nine per cell); cells with nothing below still emit nine transparent vertices; altitude matches `TerrainScatter`; all nine kernel samples taken at the CENTRE cell's drop.
**⚠ Open risk:** draw ordering is queue-decided. `MatBases.Snow` may need queue work.

# 6g. DEPTH SHRINK (`ABDepthView.cs`, UNVERIFIED IN PLAY)
The below view was geometrically correct and read as **flat levels stacked in a list**. The exponent is the accumulated drop (three levels down draws at 61%). Baked into vertices at print time. DEFAULT ON, slider 60-100%.
- **Printed things:** `FinishNewVerts` does shrink-about-`TrueCenter` and the `drop` translate in ONE pass, scale first. Operates on a VERTEX RANGE, which is what makes it robust to foreign print injection (§6a).
- **Live pawns:** `Patch_PawnRenderer_ABBelowShrink` right-multiplies `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. Right-multiply is load-bearing; a left multiply slides every below pawn towards the map origin.
- **⚠ The atlas trap:** past `ZoomRootSize` 18 humanlikes render from a cached atlas blit that ignores `PawnDrawParms.matrix`, so the scale silently evaporates at exactly the zooms used to look down a column. `Patch_PawnRenderer_ABBelowDisableCache` forces `disableCache` for below pawns only. **Verification must cross that boundary in both directions.**
- **⚠ V1's exclusion filter kept verbatim:** LINKED graphics print one quad per cell, so per-cell shrink dots a wall into a dashed line; natural rock excluded BY DEF (`mineable`/`isNaturalRock`) not by link type, because Better Mountains swaps rock to non-linked `Graphic_Random` wholesale (V1 run #50).
- Baked, so a settings change needs `RegenerateEverythingNow` - once in `ABMod.WriteSettings`.
- **Not tinted.** `SectionLayer_ABBelowLighting` already shades below content; a tint on top is the double-darkening that made V1's sky view murky.
- **ReGrowth does NOT contest this.** Its `Printer_Plane` work transpiles `Graphic_Linked.Print` + 3 subclasses ONLY, no-op unless their `printingSnow` flag is set, and our filter already skips linked graphics. Disjoint by construction.

**⚠ PERSPECTIVE MODE WAS BUILT AND REMOVED. Do not re-add it as polish.** A camera-anchored contraction as a per-frame `Matrix4x4`. It worked and was cheap. Cut once the shrink was seen in play: the shrink alone carried the depth read, and perspective bought a second cue at the price of a real artifact (no occlusion exists between a band's floor and the level below, so content slid out from under the near lip). Re-opening needs a NEW reason and must re-solve the six-pass coupling.

# 7. PER-LEVEL CHARACTER
Ore `x(1 + 0.45*(depth-1))`, cave openness `x(1 + 0.35*(depth-1))`, applied AFTER the settings clamp. **The ore multiplier scales `basementOreDensity` and is consumed by our OWN `ABOreGen.ScatterOres`** - NOT vanilla's `countPer10kCellsRange`, which is why GL's `AdjustMineables` cannot clobber it.
**⚠ The snow line never worked, and the comment saying it did not need to was wrong.** `SteadyEnvironmentEffectsTick` computes `outdoorMeltAmount` once per tick for the whole map and never calls `TryGetTemperatureForCell`. Dead for months behind a confident, wrong sentence.
**Climate defaults** (per colony, §17): +1 = -7, +2 = -16, +3 = -35, basement flat -6, wind x1.15 / x1.30 / x1.50. **No ceiling clamp by design.**

# 8. CAMERA
`ABCameraBounds.For(level)` keyed by LEVEL, not band index. `maxZoom` left DERIVED. `panMargin` 63.5 on every level. `Dialog_ABCameraCalibration` opens with the clamp UNLOCKED.
**The clamp and the level-switch input share `ABGuard.Camera`.** Both sit on per-frame / per-GUI-event paths, exactly where an unthrottled `Log.Error` turns a cosmetic bug into an unplayable game (§18a). If the clamp trips, band switching stops too. The view clip and curtain are NOT gated on it.

# 8a. NEW-GAME CAMERA ANCHOR (`ABBandView.LandOnColony`, UNVERIFIED IN PLAY)
`Game.InitNewGame` ends with `JumpToCurrentMapLoc(MapGenerator.PlayerStartSpot)`. On a banded map two things move the colony AFTER the spot is chosen: `RescueStrandedColonists` relocates anything the pod scatter threw across a gutter, and the carve can make the recorded spot unstandable.
**Confirmed mechanism in run #200:** `DropThingsNear failed to find a place to drop Nyx near (153, 0, 24). Dropping on random square instead.`
Fixed in two places: **upstream**, `FixPlayerStartSpot` prefers the colony's ACTUAL position; **backstop**, `ABGameComp.StartedNewGame` calls `LandOnColony`. **⚠ That hook, and only that hook, runs after vanilla's own camera jump.** `rememberedCameraPos` is written by hand too.
**⚠ OPEN:** in #200 the start spot was `z=24` on a band spanning 0-189, EXACTLY the `PodScatterMargin = 24` boundary. Vanilla's own pick landing there and my clamp pinning it there look IDENTICAL from outside. Verbose logging prints both.

# 9. GENERATION COST: DIAGNOSED AND LARGELY FIXED

## 9a. The profile stamps its own conditions
`ABGenProfile.Report` prints `TILE`, `PLAN`, a `SCOPING:` toggle line, and two censuses. It caught a changed tile on its FIRST use and voided a comparison that would otherwise have been believed. Emitted at WARNING level deliberately: single-occurrence info is filtered before it reaches the monitor.

## 9b. ⚠ THE COST IS DESTRUCTION, NOT GENERATION
Run #188: gensteps 3,972 ms, carve 20,447 ms (98.4% `Sky clear`), 74,584 things destroyed. Generation 16%, destruction 84%. **The original "scoping saves both halves" framing was WRONG.** Per-destroy price is stable across runs and tiles, so **op count is the only lever**. Mechanism is `ListerThings` removal, a linear `List.Remove` over ~100k-item lists.
**CLOSED:** carving before `FinalizeInit` is worth at most 169 ms of 24,600.

## 9c. The culprit was rock, proven by census
Run #190: 43,517 rock SUPPRESSED vs 4,939 DESTROYED of which only 238 rock. Reproduced on tiles 2, 3, 4. Stable across four tiles and three biomes.

## 9d. SHIPPED: `ABDoomedBands.cs`
Suppresses `GenSpawn.Spawn(ThingDef,...)` inside `GenStep_RocksFromGrid` for doomed SKY band cells. Safe because: **shape** (per-cell noise test, no count redistributed); **state-neutrality** (only the spawn is cancelled); **sky only**. Patched on the `ThingDef` overload so the cancel precedes `ThingMaker.MakeThing`.
**Neighbours, both checked and benign:** ReGrowth prefixes the 7-arg `Thing` overload (meteorite tagging), and our §15a `loc` rewrite sits there too. GL TRANSPILES `Generate` rather than the spawn.

## 9e. Run #196: the first basement, and the bottleneck moved
7 bands, 126x896. FillRock bands 0-2 = 2,606 ms (82% of carve); Sky clear = 301 ms (9%). **The sky side is solved. The basement is the whole cost.**
**⚠ MY OWN §9d CAUTION IS FALSIFIED.** The basement `FillRock` keep hits only **14.4%** of the time. Suppressing trades 7,113 destroys (~1.4 s) for 6,873 extra spawns (~200 ms). **Net ~1.2 s.** The shape of the reasoning was right; the magnitude was never checked, because no basement had ever run.
**Sign flip, a confirmation not a bug:** with rock suppressed, `Sky clear` per band INVERTED (rising with altitude). Rock tapers upward, so higher bands have more OPEN ground, and chunks only grow on open ground.
**Do not blanket-skip** water or coast mutators.

## 9f. Post-audit numbers (runs #205-#207)
| | pre-audit | post-audit |
|---|---|---|
| 4-band BorealForest carve | 1,243 ms (#200) | 1,108 ms (#206) |
| ms per destroy | 0.325 | 0.243 / 0.227 |
| 7-band FillRock | 2,606 ms (#196) | 1,911 ms (#207), -27% |
| 7-band total | ~5.5 s | **~4.1 s** |

**⚠ NOT PROVEN, confound stated:** every comparison crosses tiles and biomes, and #207 spawned MORE rock while destroying LESS. **The `ScatterOres` allocation fix cannot explain it** (~190 KB/band is worth a millisecond, not 695). Plausible mechanism is the mirror `ProgramState` guard. A clean number needs the same tile with the guard toggled.
**⚠ THE NEW TIERS INVALIDATE EVERY ABSOLUTE TIMING ABOVE for comparison purposes.** A 3 x 250 colony is 192,000 cells against 7 x 126's 112,896 - 1.7x - and cost tracks cell count. Re-baseline before comparing to any run before the tier change.

# 14. LESSONS
**Method.** Prove a subsystem innocent by finding a state where the suspect CANNOT EXIST. A documented rejection may be re-opened only by naming the confound that invalidated it. Change one thing per experiment. Run the diagnostic before the third theory. An exact number is a diagnosis. A beautiful fit is not evidence. Knowing when to stop is a result.
**⚠ Measure the ratio before optimising the half you assumed.** Generation was 16%, deletion 84%.
**⚠ A census beats a magnitude.** "74,584 things" is not a diagnosis; "43,517 Granite and Limestone" is.
**⚠ Stamp the experiment's conditions into its own output.** The tile stamp voided four bad comparisons.
**⚠ Evidence consistent with both hypotheses is not evidence; the discriminating experiment is usually cheap.** The persisted spinner. The `z=24` start spot. The palette pin. And now §21, where one click on the reappeared rock separates data from rendering.
**⚠ An optimisation you declined for a stated reason still owes you the number.** The basement keep hit rate was 14.4% and the decision inverted.
**⚠ When a symptom says "X is missing", ask how many PASSES X takes.**
**⚠ A correct value read for the wrong purpose looks like coverage.** Grep for the value's CONSUMER, not just its read site.
**⚠ A deleted feature's exclusion list is the expensive part.**
**⚠ Two cues for one property is one cue too many.**
**⚠ When two hooks both "run at startup", find the one that runs after the thing you are fixing.**
**⚠ Aim at the fact, not at the record of the intent.** `PlayerStartSpot` is a plan; the pawns are where the colony IS. **And `GameInitData.mapSize` IS the player's choice - re-deriving it through a lossy clamp is what broke Map Preview for three of four sizes (§6d-CLAMP).**
**⚠ A LOSSY NORMALISER IS NOT A WAY TO READ A CHOICE.** `Clamp` was correct at its own job (sanitise an arbitrary number downward) and completely wrong as an answer to "what did the user pick?" - it silently returned 190 for every input. **When a function's contract is "snap to something valid", it can never be used to RECOVER a value.** Ask whether the answer is already recorded somewhere before computing it.
**⚠ A CONSTRAINT SATISFIED BY EVERY EXAMPLE IS NOT NECESSARILY THE CONSTRAINT.** All three original sizes were 64k-2, and that was read for months as "band height must be 64k-2". The real rule was only ever that *Slot* is 64-aligned; 64k-2 is the cheapest fit, not the requirement. It cost vanilla-matched sizes until someone asked "what if we bump the size slightly?" **Derive the constraint from the mechanism, not from the set of things you already built.**
**⚠ A rule enforced by grepping for a SYNTAX only catches that syntax.**
**⚠ Duplication is how an invariant dies.** Seven copies of the see-below preamble. The coast rewrite was extracted at the THIRD consumer, not the eighth.
**⚠ A comment is not an invariant.**
**⚠ A kill switch with no call site is not a safety net, it is noise.**
**⚠ Steady-state fps hides burst cost.**
**⚠ The second consumer of a value you reshaped will not announce itself.**
**⚠ Timing that reads exactly 0.0 ms is an early return, not slow code.**
**⚠ In a foreign log, the loudest error is usually downstream.**
**⚠ A finding scoped to vanilla does not transfer to mods, even when the sentence sounds general.** Re-state the scope INSIDE the finding.
**⚠ A SHARED METHOD NAME IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A CONFLICT.** The §20 audit flagged six third-party collisions from names; reading the bodies cleared THREE outright. **False-positive rate on name-matching alone was 50%.**
**⚠ Compat work is mostly deletion.** The deliverable from a 150-mutator mod was 2 patches. Find the inheritance edge before counting the defs.
**⚠ Design for the foreign patch you have not met.** `FinishNewVerts` transforms a VERTEX RANGE rather than a known graphic, so a third-party `Thing.Print` postfix is correct in our view for free.
**⚠ Waste is often a sawtooth, not a curve.** Map size cost steps at 64-row slot boundaries; 200 wastes 21.9% while 190 wastes 1.0%. Tabulate before choosing a number.
**⚠ The thing you rounded away may be load-bearing.** Wide gutters looked like pure waste and are in fact the cheapest defence against the spatial-helper-crosses-the-seam bug class.
**Claims versus facts.** A comment asserting why something is safe to delete is a claim (§7). Re-measure the assumption you are about to build on.
**Shapes.** Classify into one of the six. A slice of a tall map is not a short map. A uniform symptom is a scale or constant, a patchy one is data. An odd/even symptom is arithmetic.
**Patching.** When N call sites share ONE linear mapping, re-aim the shared parameter. Find the ONE virtual everything funnels through - and when there is none, **wrap the DATA instead of the reader**. Patch the method that PRODUCES a value, not the one that stores it. Own the widget instead of patching the data it reads. Never put a foreign type in a patch-class signature - type `__instance` as `object`. **Suppress the callee, not the caller.** **State taken in a Prefix is released in a Finalizer, never a Postfix.** **Mirror the guard of the method you postfix.** **Repair a foreign method's output rather than reimplementing its body.** **Never clamp a Def field to fix one map** - Defs are global and shared across every map in the save.
**Engine facts.** `TerrainDef.holdSnowOrSand` defaults TRUE. Draw order inside and across SectionLayers is settled by material render QUEUE, not altitude. A null global texture falls back to the shader's default. Vanilla divides by a count without guarding zero. A spatial helper that reaches 22 rows will cross a 2-row gutter. `Banded` is FALSE for the whole of map generation. `SectionLayer` subclasses are auto-discovered by `Section`'s constructor, on EVERY map. Any type with a `Material` field needs `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]`. Statics keyed by game-scoped ids leak; use a CWT. FinalizeInit runs on a worker thread - so latches taken during generation must be `[ThreadStatic]`. Ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`. `CameraJumper.TryJump` silently returns unless `ProgramState == Playing`. **`MapDrawer.MapMeshDirty` also returns unless `ProgramState == Playing`.** Humanlike pawns past `ZoomRootSize` 18 render from an atlas blit that ignores `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. **Gensteps run with live-map bookkeeping DEFERRED, which is why the same work costs ~40x after `FinalizeInit`.** Harmony skips POSTFIXES when the original throws, but always runs FINALIZERS. **A prefix returning false skips the original but POSTFIXES STILL RUN.** **Harmony composes a prefix and a transpiler on the same method without conflict.** **The player's starting settlement is created by `ScenPart_PlayerFaction.PreMapGenerate()`, in a SEPARATE long event from `InitNewGame`.**

# 21. ⚠ OPEN BUG: FOG AND ROCKS ON SAVE RELOAD (NOT DIAGNOSED)
Reported from the published build: fog and rocks appear to regenerate after a save/load cycle.

**ELIMINATED so far** (each checked in source, none is the cause):
- `ABV2.*` settings-vs-map leakage. `ABV2.BandCount`/`SurfaceBand` derive from SETTINGS, and settings persist between colonies - so a reload with a changed plan would misbehave. **But they are properly confined to generation and preview**; every runtime consumer goes through the map's own scribed `ABBandMap`. Clean.
- Save compressibility. `CompressibilityDeciderUtility.IsSaveCompressible` records what is present; it cannot invent rock.
- Unsupported-roof collapse over carved sky bands. Sky roofs ARE cleared (`ABSkyBandGen:109`, `ABBandedGeneration:659/921`).
- Stale `RebindAfterLoad` ordering. It runs FIRST and unconditionally in `ABBandMap.FinalizeInit`.

**The two live hypotheses:**
- **(a) DATA** - something re-runs a generation-like pass on load, actually re-fogging and re-spawning.
- **(b) RENDERING** - nothing regenerated; the below-view layers redraw recomputed state after load, so it only looks like it.

**⚠ THE DISCRIMINATING OBSERVATION, ONE CLICK:** load an affected save and click a reappeared rock. **Selectable / mineable -> (a), real data.** Not selectable -> **(b)**, and the search collapses to the SectionLayer rebuild path on load. Do not write a fix before this; the two hypotheses predict identical screenshots and completely different fixes.
